title: Scoped PRD: Delegated Audit Trails, SSO Federation Mapping, and Operator KMS Provisioning
creator: Maya Chen
description: This PRD defines scope, acceptance criteria, and sign-off steps for delegated audit and key provisioning for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It clarifies SSO/SAML federation mapping rules, RBAC schema for operator roles, requirement for HSM-backed key material, and the audit evidence artifacts required for customer onboarding/SOC reviews. Goal: enable a predictable operator provisioning flow that preserves customer KMS custody guarantees while surfacing auditable operator actions and SSO assertions.
scope_inclusions: SSO/SAML assertion mapping to canonical operator identities
Operator RBAC roles and least-privilege templates
KMS/HSM provisioning workflow (escrow, split-key, automated rotation hooks)
Detailed audit event schema for operator actions, key access, and SSO sessions
Acceptance tests and evidence artifacts for customer onboarding
scope_exclusions: Custom identity providers not using SAML v2.0 (investigate separately)
Full multi-tenant key sharing (out of scope, addressed by future initiative)
Migration tooling for legacy operator accounts (separate migration ticket)
success_metrics: Zero failed audits due to missing fields in 3rd-party customer onboarding tests
Ability to replay operator actions for 90 days of logs in staging
Automated KMS provisioning end-to-end in < 15 minutes in test harness
SAML assertion-to-role mapping verified by >90% of pilot customers
acceptance_criteria: Conformance tests: SAML assertion fields (Subject, NameID, Attributes) map to canonical operator ID with documented transformation rules
RBAC: Templates for 'operator-readonly', 'operator-maintain', 'operator-admin' created and enforced in local RBAC engine
KMS/HSM: Provisioning flow documented; HSM-backed keys created in customer-managed KMS and a public attest token returned
Audit logs: Every operator API call emits structured JSON event with timestamp, operator_id, request_id, action, resource, and kms_key_id
Evidence: Confluence onboarding checklist + sample audit export + signed HSM attestation uploaded to customer onboarding folder
Security review: Design doc has annoted threat model and mitigation plan and Security signoff present in reviewers list
qa_tests: End-to-end onboarding runbook executed against a staging VPC using a test IdP (SAML) - record results
Fault injection: simulate KMS unavailable and verify failover path and no plaintext key leakage
RBAC fuzz: attempt privilege escalation via malformed SAML attributes and assert denial
Audit integrity: tamper simulation - verify log immutability hooks (checksum/signature) detect changes
signoff_checklist: Security reviews and signs off on threat model and KMS/HSM ops
Infra/Automation approves provisioning playbook and rollback steps
Design verifies identity attribute mapping and UI flows
Customer Ops confirms onboarding evidence artifacts sufficient for SOC review
decisions: Use SAML v2.0 as mandatory IdP protocol; OIDC/OAuth2 postponed
Operator RBAC will be implemented as declarative templates with policy-as-code in the console
KMS integration supports both AWS KMS and customer HSM via KMIP adapter; initial implementation will prioritize HSM attestation for high-risk customers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: SAML attribute variability across IdPs -> Mitigation: canonical mapping table with fallbacks and per-customer overrides
Risk: HSM attestation complexity -> Mitigation: provide a shim that returns a standardized attestation token and test harness
Risk: Audit volume at scale -> Mitigation: sampling tier for debug-level events and compressed archival path
